name: Better Data for AI is Everyone's Job
description:
**PLEASE REGISTER ON THE DAMA PHILADELPHIA [WEBSITE](https://damaphila.starchapter.com/meetinginfo.php?id=51&ts=1790867055) TO RECEIVE THE CORRECT ZOOM LINK FOR THE EVENT**

**11am-12pm EST:** **Terri Mikol -** Data & Analytics Governance Advisor.
Better Data is Everyone's Job
Organizations know they need data governance for analytics and AI, but often lack the time, budget, or resources to launch another major program. This session presents a practical approach that uses the organization's existing people, skills, processes, and technology to improve data quality, clarify ownership, increase data literacy, and build sustainable governance without a large investment.
**12pm-12:30pm EST:** **Marilu Lopez** the owner and CEO of SEGDA company
Most organizations face pressure to extract value from their data. They often jump straight into implementing MDM initiatives, moving to the cloud, adopting advanced analytics, and now, integrating AI, without a solid understanding of the problems they need to solve or the priorities involved. However, there is a growing awareness of the importance of managing data more effectively, even though the path to achieving this remains unclear. A Data Strategy is essential for setting priorities and guiding resource allocation effectively. This session explains how to develop Data Strategies using the PAC (Pragmatic, Agile, and Communicable) Data Strategy Method.
Create your Data Strategies with the right stakeholders in a pragmatic, agile way, and communicate them effectively using a Canvas.
**12:30 - 1:15pm EST:** **Swati Prasad** \- Senior Manager\, Enterprise Data Governance — American Express\. Founder\, DataTrustHub \| Creator\, DataPolis\.
Policy as Code, Compliance as a Token
Swati Prasad serves as Senior Manager of Enterprise Data Governance at American Express, where she leads initiatives focused on data quality, risk controls, and regulatory compliance frameworks. She is the founder and primary contributor to DataTrustHub, an online publication exploring real-world data governance, and creator of DataPolis, a storytelling series designed to make DAMA-DMBOK2 standards accessible across organizations. Her recent research work focuses on integrating smart contracts, pre-chain validation, and distributed ledger technologies to eliminate manual control vulnerabilities and establish authoritative single sources of truth for enterprise analytics and AI.
Data governance depends on custodians who verify where data came from and whether it followed policy. Today that verification happens after the fact, from metadata attached to the data set, which makes audits slow and leaves compliance failures to be found late.
This talk proposes moving verification into the data lifecycle itself. At each stage, a smart contract confirms that the relevant organizational policy was followed and issues a token as proof. The contract relies on an oracle, and the right oracle depends on how subjective the policy is: software code for objective rules, a decentralized committee for judgment calls, or a gatekeeper where accountability must rest with a named party. The final certification checks the full chain of tokens and attests to the compliance of the data. Because each token acts as a micro compliance record that is decentralized and independently verifiable, regulators can audit the record directly instead of relying on the custodian's account of it. The core argument is that policy written as code, paired with oracles matched to the policy, shifts governance from retrospective inspection to continuous proof, and makes the choice of oracle the central governance decision.

# ☕ The OG Coffee&Code Meetup

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”
This is **The OG Coffee&Code**—the meetup that started it all, now presented in collaboration with the **Blockspace Community**.
No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

## What this meetup is

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

## What this meetup is not

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

## How it works

1. Show up

3. Open your laptop, notebook, or sketchpad
4. Work at your own pace
5. Chat when you want and focus when you need
6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

## Who should attend

* Software engineers and data professionals
* Students and self-learners

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.
This collaboration brings together two communities around a shared goal: creating a relaxed, supportive space where people can build, learn, and connect.

**Come for the code.**
**Stay for the community.**
**Leave caffeinated. ☕🚀**

name: Emerging Research in Cislunar Space and How to Get Involved
description:
This workshop will introduce NASA’s upcoming Artemis missions, emerging research areas in cislunar space, and opportunities for programmers, engineers, students, and space enthusiasts to contribute to humanity’s return to the Moon. Participants will learn the fundamentals of orbital motion, reference frames, trajectory design, and orbit propagation before exploring current research in cislunar space situational awareness, lunar landing and descent, and space robotics. The session will conclude with a short Python demonstration of selenocentric orbit propagation using planetary ephemerides.
The workshop will be led by Scott Blender, a third-year Ph.D. student in aerospace engineering at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) and a researcher in the Advanced Space Concepts Laboratory. His research focuses on spacecraft guidance, cislunar space domain awareness, and lunar-surface sensor networks. He previously interned at AstronetX, a startup developing an optical system for cislunar space situational awareness.

The workshop will be organized as follows:

1. NASA’s Return to the Moon Through Artemis
2. Fundamentals of Orbital Motion: Kepler’s Laws and Newtonian Gravitation
3. Two-Body Orbit Propagation, Reference Frames, and Selenocentric Orbits
4. Emerging Cislunar Research: Space Situational Awareness, Lunar Landing and Descent, and Space Robotics
5. Live Python Demonstration: Ephemeris-Supported Orbit Propagation
6. Q&A and Opportunities to Get Involved

description:
## **Join Philadelphia's leading community for AI, SaaS & Technology growth.**

Please register here: https://luma.com/wbaeeeaw

​Our mission is to build the #1 community for founders, operators, executives, investors, and builders growing AI-first SaaS, technology, and innovation-driven companies, through real relationships, shared learning, and growth-focused collaboration.
​Every Meetup delivers intentional networking, actionable insights, and direct access to leaders who know what it takes to grow, fund, scale, and exit in today's competitive market.
​If you're serious about building in AI, SaaS, or Tech, this is where you belong.

​**Healthcare AI: Product Development from Concept to Launch**
​Healthcare is one of the hardest places to ship AI: a product has to fit real clinical workflows and earn the trust of the people using it. Chris Cera will walk through how a healthcare idea becomes a validated, launch-ready product, including where AI solves a real problem and how to pressure-test an idea before investing heavily.
​Whether you're validating a healthcare idea, adding AI to an existing product, or evaluating digital health as an investor, you'll leave with practical ideas you can apply to your business.

​About the Speaker
​**Chris Cera, CEO, Arcweb Technologies**
​Chris leads Arcweb Technologies, a Philadelphia-based Certified B Corp and AI product studio that has helped more than 100 organizations build digital health products. He previously co-founded Vuzit (acquired by Accusoft) and Philly Startup Leaders, and holds B.S. and M.S. degrees in Computer Science from Drexel University.

description:

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.
* Project Lightwell: How automated, validated patching and backports maintain enterprise stability in an AI-accelerated threat landscape.
* Peer Networking: Connect with local IT leaders and Red Hat experts over food and drinks at Philly's newest high-energy venue.

[Event Details:](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451)

* Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
* Time: 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM ET
* Location: F1 Arcade Philadelphia \| 1330 Chestnut St\, Philadelphia\, PA 19107

Don't miss this opportunity to transform your security posture while networking with industry peers.
Have questions? Reach out to us at rhug@redhat.com.
We look forward to seeing you there!
Best regards,
The Red Hat User Group Team

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.
